title: Google broadens its AI hardware portfolio with two new specialized chips
slides: Google quietly shifts its AI hardware strategy—why now?
Two chips target training and inference separately.
One chip is not a TPU and changes the game.
Your cloud AI costs could drop if you adopt early.
Audit your workload: which chip fits your stack?
thread_text:
1. The AI chip shift nobody saw coming

Google just split its AI hardware into two chips: one for training, one for inference. The inference chip isn't a TPU. That changes cloud AI economics.

2. Why split training and inference?

Training needs raw power. Inference needs efficiency. One chip can't do both well. Google's new split targets each workload separately, cutting waste.

3. Not a TPU. A game changer.

The inference chip abandons TPU architecture entirely. That means Google can optimize for latency and cost per query, not just raw throughput.

4. Your cloud bill could shrink.

Early adopters of the inference chip may see lower costs per AI request. If you run large-scale inference, the savings compound fast.

5. Audit your workload now.

Which chip fits your stack? Map your training vs inference usage this week. If you haven't checked, start there.

Google just split its AI chips into two: one for training, one for inference.

If you run large-scale inference, your cloud bill per AI request could shrink — and savings compound fast.
